There is extensive evidence that there is far more to the brain than simply replicating these connections. Consider that in the 90's it was all the rage to say the same thing about genetics as we conducted the human genome project. Once that data was actually put into play it became clear that the whole endeavor is far more complex than imagined. Articles that suggest otherwise are typically back-door hype for some industry.

We're getting down the fundamentals now though, or the latest fundamentals at least. Enough accuracy to start adjusting brain function during run time and with no as yet recorded side effects. In another 15 years when the human genome is actually fully accounted for and the brain is mapped and reverse engineered I don't see why we couldn't have sentient AIs. The only thing that's holding us back is the same thing that held us back when we sequenced our genome, computing power.
